description.narrative: Det övergripande målet med interventionen är att främja säkra, hållbara och värdiga levnadsvillkor för fördrivna människor i konfliktdrabbade områden. Projektet syftar till att stärka användandet av landtillgångar och samtidigt stärka samhälles möjligheter att använda land för inkomstbringande aktiviteter. Projektet avses implementeras i delstaterna Södra Kordofan och White Nile.

The overall objective of the intervention is to foster safe, sustainable, and dignified living conditions for displacement-affected communities prone to conflict over natural resources and due to inadequate adaptable and diversified livelihood options resulting in additional barrier in accessing basic services. The project will be implemented in South Kordofan State and White Nile State.

The overall objective of the CASPIR project is improved peaceful, sustainable, and dignified living conditions for displacement-affected communities as result of enhanced, diversified, and more adaptable livelihoods productivity, enhanced financial inclusion and strengthened market systems.
The specific outcome objectives are:
Outcome 1: Support pathways towards sustainable peace through a more inclusive, community centred process with greater participation of women.; and
Outcome 2: Support to agriculture production systems through sustainable and diversified practices to foster increased production, food security, and access to markets.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The following is a summary of progress extracted from projects interim narrative report covering the period from May 2023 to April 2024. Originally, the project was to be implemented in South Kordofan and North Darfur. However, due to the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces in North Darfur, which made the area inaccessible, White Nile State was added as a project location while activities in North Darfur remain suspended. Work in White Nile began after September 2023, with an inception period agreed upon to assess the needs in the area and plan for the subsequent years of the project.
Progress under project objective 1 Support pathways towards sustainable peace through a more inclusive, community-centred process with greater participation of women
An assessment has been conducted of Information, Counselling, and Legal Assistance (ICLA) priority needs of displacement affected populations in White Nile with a specific focus on gaps related to access to Legal identity including Civil Documentation (LCD), Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) disputes as it relates to access to land for agricultural purposes and dispute resolution. The findings of the assessment informs the needed amendments to the project and as well provides evidence-based advocacy for stakeholders on existing gaps, defining responsive interventions and identifying a response priority for the project.
In White Nile, NRC conducted a mapping of Collaborative Dispute Resolution (CDR) structures and a comprehensive Conflict Analysis in the period between February to March 2024. This effort was part of the ICLA needs assessment. The ICLA assessment aimed to identify key gaps and priorities for program implementation, covering Guli, Kosti, and Rabak localities using quantitative methods. The findings include for example that for 67% of respondents, cost is the main barrier to accessing these documents, followed by the distance to registration centers, lack of supporting documents, and limited awareness. Other challenges include risks of conflict on routes, complicated procedures, and insufficient information on where to seek assistance. The main HLP issues are tenancy (38%) and eviction (6%). Community dispute resolution structures emerged as the predominant method for resolving disputes, with 36% of respondents frequently using them, followed by 21% who opt for the court system. The findings affirmed the relevance of planned interventions focusing on providing information, counselling, legal aid, and community-based conflict resolution approaches.
A stakeholder analysis in South Kordofan and White Nile States identified key and influential players, which aided in formulating an engagement strategy with community leaders, selecting project participants, and mitigating potential intercommunal tensions during the selection process.
NRC conducted a Gender Analysis assessment in South Kordofan and White Nile revealing significant gaps in education, employment, health, and decision-making affecting women. These gaps contribute to unequal access to HLP rights for women. To address these issues, targeted interventions are necessary to promote gender equality and empower women in these regions. In White Nile State, women generally participate actively in humanitarian aid and development programs, often more so than men. However, rural women encounter logistical and cultural barriers, such as needing male approval to attend programs.
Progress under project objective 2 Support to agro-pastoralist production systems through sustainable and diversified practices to foster increased production, food security, and access to markets
To inform the mapping of sustainable agro-pastoral livelihoods options, NRC conducted six community mobilization meetings to communicate project objectives in Murta North, Alshaeir Almtar, and Alshaeir Almuskar. Around 400 participants attended these meetings to discuss the high-level implementation plan and enhance their engagement with the project. They proposed the selection criteria for project participation. Based on these criteria, the NRC selected 200 beneficiaries, 60% of whom are women from Murta North, Alshaeir Almtar, and Alshaeir Almuskr. Half of these beneficiaries are experiencing protracted displacement. NRC trained 24 lead farmers to serve as trainers and extension agents for the project's eight farmers' field schools (FFS). The participants selected eight demonstration sites, totaling 16 feddans, with 2 feddans per FFS. They chose sorghum, both local and improved varieties, as the main food security crop to reduce the risks associated with rainfall variability. For cash crops, they selected both improved and local varieties of groundnuts and sesame, considering the potential for value addition. Cow beans were also chosen for their dual role as a food security crop and a cash crop. The FFS will introduce recent production practices Farm management, Pest control, planting calendar , cost /profit analysis, Water Harvesting techniques and post-harvest lose management showing differences between farmers own knowledge and practices with scientific method.
NRC conducted a Nexus Environmental Assessment to identify the environmental risks associated with the intervention. Based on the analysis, NRC recommended adopting agroforestry techniques and agro-pastoral initiatives, which incorporate climate adaptation measures and can enhance community resilience, environmental awareness, and crop diversification. NRC supported the establishment of three natural resource management committees in three locations and provided interactive sessions adopting theoretical and practical approaches on environmental risks, natural resource management, community environmental action planning, etc.
In White Nile, NRC conducted a comprehensive livelihood assessment through a consultant, that utilized qualitative and quantitative methods to scope viable livelihoods and food security opportunities for refuges, host community, and IDPs. The findings highlight both opportunities and challenges across various livelihood sectors.
NRC conducted a seed security assessment in Kadugli and Ar Reif Ash Shargi localities in South Kordofan, revealing that 90% of the households interviewed are seed insecure for the upcoming sowing season. This insecurity stems primarily from the previous season's security issues and poor harvests caused by poor rains and locusts. The assessment recommended key interventions, including the provision of agricultural inputs such as seeds and tools, as well as capacity-building initiatives for recipients.
During the reporting period, NRC conducted a total of 203 sessions on legal identity and civil documentation (LID), reaching a total of 4,886 individuals (3,731F, 1,155M) in South Kordofan. In White Nile, NRC conducted seven group information sessions on LID and counselling on LID and HLP to inform and empower project participants to make informed decisions and access their rights. Additionally, NRC conducted a survey to assess and analyse the priority needs of displacement-affected populations regarding access to legal identity, civil documentation, and HLP disputes related to land access for agricultural purposes and dispute resolution.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
